Optional
Coding agents and working locally
← Start here

<marimo-callout-output data-html='"\u003cspan class=\"markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"paragraph\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThis page is optional, and most students never need it.\u003c/strong\u003e Everything the course requires runs in\nmolab, in your browser, with nothing to install, and any AI chat can write the code for you. This page\nis for anyone curious to try a \u003cstrong\u003ecoding agent\u003c/strong\u003e (such as Claude Code) that works on a notebook directly,\nor to run the notebooks on their own computer. It earns no extra credit, nothing is graded differently,\nand you can stop any time.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-kind='"info"'></marimo-callout-output>

data.text/markdown:
Two optional routes

  • A. Connect a coding agent to a molab notebook. Your notebook stays in molab; the agent runs on your computer and edits the notebook for you. This is the easier route if you want to try an agent.
  • B. Run marimo on your computer. The notebook itself runs on your computer. Try this only if you want to work offline or without molab.
Before you start
  • There are steps for Mac and Windows: pick your tab wherever you see one.
  • You'll type a few commands in Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell (Windows). You don't need to understand them: copy each one exactly.
  • This is self-supported. Classmates and the class channel can help, but class time stays on the course work. If something doesn't work, carry on in molab with an AI chat; that always works.
  • Read the data rule on your own computer (below) before you start an agent.

data.text/html:
Set up your computer (once)

  1. Open Terminal: press ⌘ Space, type Terminal, press Return.
  2. Install uv, a small free tool that installs Python and the packages a notebook needs: 
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  3. Install Node.js (route A needs its npx command): download the LTS installer from nodejs.org and run it. If you already use Homebrew, brew install node works too.
  4. Install a coding agent. Claude Code is paid (it needs a Claude subscription or API account); check claude.com/claude-code for current instructions. At the time of writing: 
    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Codex and OpenCode also work; molab shows the commands for each.
  1. Make a course folder, and keep only course files in it: 
    mkdir -p ~/DATA6900
  2. Close Terminal and open it again. Type uv --version, npx --version and claude --version; each should print a version number.
  1. Open PowerShell: press the Windows key, type PowerShell, press Enter. (Not "Command Prompt".)
  2. Install Git for Windows from git-scm.com and accept the default options. Claude Code and the agent connection both need it.
  3. Install uv, a small free tool that installs Python and the packages a notebook needs: 
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
  4. Install Node.js (route A needs its npx command): download the LTS installer (.msi) from nodejs.org and run it with the default options.
  5. Install a coding agent. Claude Code is paid (it needs a Claude subscription or API account); check claude.com/claude-code for current instructions. At the time of writing: 
    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
Codex and OpenCode also work; molab shows the commands for each.
  1. Make a course folder, and keep only course files in it: 
    mkdir $HOME\DATA6900
  2. Close PowerShell and open it again. Type uv --version, npx.cmd --version and claude --version; each should print a version number.

data.text/markdown:
Give the agent your rules (once)

Claude Code reads a file called CLAUDE.md in the folder you start it from. Save this as CLAUDE.md in your course folder (~/DATA6900 on a Mac, C:\Users\<you>\DATA6900 on Windows) and make it yours; the "Going further" items in weeks 3 and 10 ask you to add your grain and your citation rule. Always start the agent from inside your course folder. 
# DATA 6900 course folder

## Data rule

- Only public, aggregate data (CMS, CDC, the course mirror). Never PHI, patient-level data, or anything from my job.

- Work only inside this folder. Don't read files outside it.

- Never ask for, print or save API keys or passwords.

## How to work

- Show me your plan before you change a notebook, and wait for me to agree.

- After every join, print the row counts before and after.

- "Not Available" and other text in a number column means missing, never zero. Say how many rows are missing.

- When you report a number, say which source and which reporting period it comes from.

- Explain what you changed in plain language, for someone who doesn't code.

Route A: connect a coding agent to a molab notebook

  1. In molab, open your own copy of the notebook (click Fork, or Save a copy while it runs) and run it. Changes an agent makes to the read-only preview aren't saved.
  2. Open the ☰ menu at the top right of the notebook and choose Connect your agent. A window called Pair with an agent opens. Pick the tab for your agent (for example Claude).
  3. Step 1 in that window, once per computer: copy the install command and run it in Terminal or PowerShell. It adds the marimo-pair skill, which teaches the agent how to work in a marimo notebook. On Windows, type npx.cmd where the command says npx. 
    npx skills add marimo-team/marimo-pair
  4. Step 2: go to your course folder (cd ~/DATA6900 on a Mac, cd $HOME\DATA6900 on Windows), then paste the command copied from the window, which starts with claude, and press Return. Copy it from molab, not from this page: it contains your notebook's address, and it changes each time you start the notebook.
  5. Step 3: before the agent starts, Terminal asks for a token. Copy it from the window (the copy button next to the stars) and paste it. The token is a key to your running notebook: don't share it, post it, or put it in a notebook. It stays in a temporary file on your computer, not in the chat, and only works while that notebook session is running.
  6. Claude Code starts, connects, and usually pops up a short message in your molab notebook to say it's ready. It asks your permission before it runs commands: read what it wants to do before you say yes.
  7. Ask for something small first. The week 1 Ask your AI prompt works well: paste it into the agent and watch the new cell appear in molab. Check its work the same way you'd check an AI chat's code.
Your work stays in your molab copy, so you submit its link as usual. To stop, type /exit in the agent.

data.text/html:
Route B: run marimo on your computer

Each course notebook is a single file. For week 1:
cd ~/DATA6900
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fairfield-dolan-healthcare-analytics/healthcare-analytics-course-data/main/course2027/notebooks/week01_first_chart.py
uvx marimo edit --sandbox week01_first_chart.py

cd $HOME\DATA6900
curl.exe -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fairfield-dolan-healthcare-analytics/healthcare-analytics-course-data/main/course2027/notebooks/week01_first_chart.py
uvx marimo edit --sandbox week01_first_chart.py
For another week, change the file name in the last two lines (the names are in the Start page links). marimo opens in your browser. The first time takes a minute or two while uv installs Python and the notebook's packages; after that it starts quickly.
  • Always include --sandbox. It installs exactly the packages the notebook lists, so your numbers match everyone's on molab.
  • To stop marimo, go back to Terminal or PowerShell and press Control-C.
  • The notebook loads the same dated course data as molab and keeps a copy in a data folder next to it.
  • Your changes are saved in the .py file in your course folder.
  • Started in molab? Download your notebook from molab as a .py file, put it in your course folder, and open that file instead.
  • To add an agent, use Connect your agent in the ☰ menu, the same way as route A.
Submitting: deliverables are still molab links that a classmate can open without installing anything. Upload your .py file to your molab workspace, check that it runs there, and submit that link. Don't submit a .py file or an HTML export.

data.text/markdown:
The data rule, on your own computer

The rule doesn't change: only public, aggregate data. A coding agent adds one thing to watch. A chat assistant only sees what you paste into it; an agent on your computer can read any file it can reach, and once it's connected to a molab notebook it can copy what it reads into that notebook, which may be shared.
  • Work only inside your course folder, and start the agent from inside it.
  • Don't use a work computer for this course. Your employer's rules come first, and a work laptop is where patient data and work files live.
  • Never put API keys, passwords or connection tokens in the course folder or in a notebook.
  • If you aren't sure whether a file counts, keep the agent away from it.

Transcripts

If this is one of your transcript weeks, Claude Code's /export command saves the session. See the transcript guide for what to submit.

If something goes wrong

  • command not found (Mac) or is not recognized (Windows) for uv, npx or claude: close Terminal or PowerShell and open it again. If it's still missing, repeat that install step.
  • Windows: "running scripts is disabled on this system": type npx.cmd instead of npx.
  • Windows: the Step 2 command fails in PowerShell: open Git Bash (installed with Git for Windows), go to your course folder with cd ~/DATA6900, and paste the command there.
  • No "Connect your agent" in the ☰ menu: you're looking at the read-only preview. Open your own copy and run it.
  • The agent can't reach the notebook: the notebook session ended or restarted. Open Connect your agent again and copy the new command and token.
  • The browser didn't open (route B): copy the http://localhost link that Terminal or PowerShell printed into your browser.
  • Anything else: carry on in molab with an AI chat, and ask in the class channel if you want to keep trying.
